summary_html: Agency places a child with **relatives or kin caregivers** instead of non-relative foster care. Federal law favors kinship care as least-restrictive, family-preserving placement.

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. A.W.
key_cases.holding: Reversing termination, the Court set out the four-part best-interests standard for terminating parental rights under N.J.S.A. 30:4C-15(c) and held the Division must prove it by clear and convincing evidence.
key_cases.relevance: A.W. states that when a relative is willing to provide long-term care, termination is 'unnecessary and unwise,' making relative placement a required alternative to consider.
key_cases.quote: The child's health and development have been or will be seriously impaired by the parental relationship.

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. P.P.
key_cases.holding: The Court held kinship legal guardianship is available only when adoption is neither feasible nor likely, so it cannot be raised as a defense to termination where a relative is willing to adopt.
key_cases.relevance: P.P. explains the statutory role of kinship caregivers and when their care becomes a permanent legal arrangement.
key_cases.quote: when the permanency provided by adoption is available, kinship legal guardianship cannot be used as a defense to termination of parental rights under N.J.S.A. 30:4C-15.1a(3)

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. K.L.W.
key_cases.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
key_cases.holding: The court reversed a termination judgment because the Division failed to comply with its statutory duty under N.J.S.A. 30:4C-12.1 to identify and assess relatives, which distorted the best-interests analysis.
key_cases.relevance: K.L.W. is the leading New Jersey decision on the Division's duty to locate, notify and assess relatives as placement resources.
key_cases.quote: The Division has a statutory obligation to contact relatives of a child in its custody.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed Congress's constitutional authority to enact the Indian Child Welfare Act and reversed on the anticommandeering claims, vacating and remanding the equal-protection and nondelegation claims with instructions to dismiss for lack of standing.
key_cases.relevance: Brackeen restates that ICWA requires a state court to place an Indian child with an Indian caretaker when one is available, controlling kinship and tribal placement decisions.
key_cases.quote: But the bottom line is that we reject all of petitioners' challenges to the statute, some on the merits and others for lack of standing.

common_failures: Failure to consider less restrictive alternatives

timeline_requirements.deadline: Hearing on the next court day (the Division must cause a complaint to be filed within two court days after the removal, N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.30(b))
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Child's emergency (“Dodd”) removal from the home without a court order
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: If there has been no hearing on the removal at which the parent or guardian was present or had an adequate opportunity to be present, the parent or guardian may apply for a hearing on returning the child, which must be held within three court days of the application except for good cause shown (N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.32).

notice_requirements.timing: At least 24 hours before the court hearing (reasonable effort by the Division)

statutory_basis.citation_text: N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.30(a) (the Division shall make a reasonable effort, at least 24 hours prior to the court hearing, to notify the parent or guardian of the time to appear in court and to inform the parent or guardian of the right to obtain counsel, and how to obtain counsel through the Office of the Public Defender if indigent)
